## 2026-10-23 — 197. A Newton update that has stopped contracting is judged against the rounding its own solve carries -- a user's 4 mV supply step, which fell to the minimum step at the step's corner, completes in 0.07 s (the 2 mV step's waveform within 1.6e-11 V)

**Why**  The step test of 196 (a 4 mV step into an op-amp macromodel's supply; reltol 1e-9, iabstol 1e-13) failed
because one update could not settle: a 0 V source's current in the macromodel, set by the KCL of a node a 354 pF
capacitor loads.  At a small step the capacitor's companion makes that KCL a difference of terms ~C/h |v|, and
the residual is evaluated to eps of them, so the current moves by ~eps C |v| / h every iteration -- 7e-8 A at
h = 1e-18 s against a tolerance of 1e-13 A -- while the residual's own test holds.  It crosses the tolerance at
h ~ 1e-12 s, where the failures began; each retry halved h and doubled the noise, down to `minstep`.  The current
is not a capacitive loop's (the node's other side is a state through 1 ohm), so the error test's 'charge' mode is
right to leave it alone: what failed is the Newton's update test, which no tolerance setting reaches.  The 2 mV
step converged only because each such Newton happened to draw a noise sample under the tolerance.

**Built.**  `StandardNewton`'s fourth condition (`nrsolver._within_rounding`): where the residual's test holds,
no stateful limiter limited, and the update fails and has stopped contracting (its largest entry not under half
the last one's: `_step_size`), every unknown failing the update test passes if it moved by less than its
tolerance plus ``eps (|J^-1| I_scale)_i`` -- the residual's own scale (``|J| |x_next| + |F|``) through row i of
J^-1.  The rows by transposed solves with the failing unknowns' unit vectors, `FLOOR_ROWS` (32) at a time, on the
factorisation the step was just solved with (`LinearSolver.solve_transposed`, new: numpy's solve of J^T on a
dense J, `klu_tsolve` on the numeric `StructuralKLU` refactored; numpy's solve of J^T where a scaler
equilibrated the step), each floor ``eps * np.dot(|row|, I_scale)``.  A Newton that converges by (1)-(3) is
untouched; the floor is consulted only on a stall.  Accepted, the point is as good as the arithmetic allows: the
residual's test, which holds, already bounds its error by reltol / eps (~4.5e6) times this floor.  The C Newtons
make it bit for bit: newton.c (`step_size`, `floor_holds`; the dense rows by dgesv on J reduced row-major --
J^T's column-major copy -- the KLU rows by klu_tsolve on the run's numeric; the floors by numpy's own ddot) and
dcnewton.c (the same, its flags read before the verdict); `_tran_newton_c._chain` and `_dc_newton_c` take the
Python where either helper is patched.

**Measured** on the peer's case (scratch only; its macromodels are vendor files), every failing Newton before
this change: over 217 000 stalled iterations the observed moves were 0.023 (median) .. 0.27 (max) of the floor;
the moves above it were genuine first steps from the predictor, which the floor refuses (it needs a stall).
After: the 4 mV step passes (309 steps, 15 rejected, 666 Newton iterations; 0.07 s with the C, the Python's
bytes); the 2 mV step's three node waveforms move by at most 1.6e-11 V (tolerance ~2e-9 V), 515 Newton
iterations against 525.

**Tests.**  test_nrsolver_variants: an update at its residual's rounding converges at the second iteration, one
11x over the floor is refused; a contracting update never consults the floor; one block or two, the same answer.
test_structural_klu: the transposed solve is on the numeric the solve left (numpy's to the rounding, nothing
factored or counted again; a foreign matrix answered by the fallback).  test_newton_c: a VCVS-and-354 pF chain at
femtosecond steps, dense and on KLU -- the C's bytes, statistics and warnings the Python's, whose Newtons the
floor converged.  test_dc_newton_c: the stalled step as an operating point (a behavioural g V for the companion, a
current source for its history), dense and on KLU (130 cells, five blocks) -- the C's bytes the Python's, and

result is held (`_tran_radau_c.hold`) and the next `solve` serves it once where its inputs are the same bytes
and the stage KLU and limiter walk as held -- without it, a Newton that factored afresh is repeated as a
refactor of what it left (forced: refactors / factors 170 / 1 against the Python's 168 / 3); after the step map
the step is made and the glue does what the Python does next (`advance` at full width, the LinAlgError).  The
step map writes to the one of two buffers the carried `P` is not in; a point whose reference entry is not +0.0
stops (the next step starts from the inserted +0.0); a constant `C` is screened (the Python's kept verdict is
the same screen).  `_walk_stage` resumes the C after a step it stopped before, and spaces out calls that made
none (1, 2, 4 ... 64 Python steps).  `_sensklu_c.full_step` factored out of `step` for the full-width step.
Serves what the C stage Newton serves on the walk's KLU: no stateful limiter, no PCNR, the cost transform off.

## 2026-10-24 — 209. The complex KLU solver frees what it replaces -- `ComplexKLUSolver` and the C stepping loop's transform mode: voter25's peak memory 448 -> 390 MB, every byte the same

**Why**  Found building 208 (Andreas: fix it): `ComplexKLUSolver.solve_prepared` overwrote its analysis and factor at a
new pattern, and its factor at a residual fallback, without freeing either -- a voter25 Radau run left 1 152 of each
(a new pattern every eight attempts), mux8 912 patterns and 94 fallbacks -- and the C stepping loop's transform mode
(208) mirrored it.

**Built.**  `ComplexKLUSolver._free_numeric` / `_free_symbolic` (`klu_z_free_numeric`, `klu_free_symbolic`, declared
with its other entries): at a new key the factor and the analysis it holds are freed before the new analysis; at a
residual fallback the factor before the fresh one; at the solver's end (`__del__`) both.  `analyses_freed` and
`factors_freed` count the first two.  loop.c's `tc_kept`: a made attempt's new pattern (an attempt judged, or abandoned
at the early abort) frees the analysis and factor it replaced; an attempt handed back frees its own and puts the old
back (`tc_undo`), as before.  Its counts (`tc_symfreed`, `tc_numfreed`) are settled into the solver by
`_tran_tcloop_c._settle`, which now runs however the call ends.  The holders of the handles compare them with the
solver's before each use (`_tran_radau_tc`'s key, the loop's binding key): a freed handle is never used, and a new
object at a freed address is the solver's own.

**Not changed (found).**  `KLUSolver.solve` (real) overwrites its analysis and factor the same way at a new pattern
and a residual fallback.  Its handles are borrowed by four C units (`_tran_newton_c`, `_dc_newton_c`, `_pcnr_c`,
`_tran_lte_c`), each its own audit before a free can be added: an item of its own.

**Measured.**  voter25 under Radau, each tree from its own directory: peak RSS 448 -> 390 MB (the run's growth 154 ->
95 MB), 1 152 analyses and 1 152 factors freed, one of each left; 17.0 s both.

## 2026-10-24 — 211. The transform's fallback in C left the dense Newton's record on the loop's buffers -- a fallback the Python made after the C's read the C's last attempt's charge, sources and seeds

**Found**  210's fallback twin, run alone (the first transient of a fresh process), counted otherwise: one fallback's
dense Newton not converging where the Python-only run's did; the waveform the same, the Python's own Newton then
converging.  210's glue let the C point the transient's `_radau_c` record's inputs and outputs (`qn`, `u`, `seed`,
`Ya` ...) at the loop's buffers and left them there; `_tran_radau_c.solve` writes its own buffers, set once at the
record's making, and the C read the loop's.  A Python fallback after the C's -- here where a cold process split the
attempts otherwise -- read the C's last attempt's charge, sources and seeds; a Newton converging on them would have
handed back another step's stages.  207's glue saves and restores them around its call; 210's did not.  The gold decks
never met it: past a deck's first fallback every one was the C's.

**Fixed**  `_tran_tcloop_c._call` saves the record's pointers before the C and restores them after, as
`_tran_stageloop_c._call` does.

**Tests**  test_tcloop_c (+2, 29): after the C's fallbacks the record's `qn`, `u` and `seed` its own buffers; the
fixed-grid fallback twin in a fresh process (the C's run its first transient) the Python's -- both failing on 210's
glue.  test_pinned_pairs: 'the transform loop and its C' re-recorded on its twin.

## 2026-10-24 — 213. The real KLU solvers free what they replace and what they hold at their end -- `KLUSolver` at a new pattern and a residual fallback, every one at its end: 2 000 pattern changes +115 -> +9 MB

**Why**  Andreas: fix the real KLU solver's leak (found at 209).  `KLUSolver.solve` overwrote its analysis and factor
at a new pattern, and its factor at a residual fallback, without freeing them; and no real KLU solver freed anything
at its end -- `solve`'s analysis and factor, `factor`'s analyses -- so each run's `StructuralKLU` (one to three a gold
deck) left its analysis and its last numeric.

**Audited**  The C units that borrow a `StructuralKLU`'s handles (`_tran_newton_c`, `_dc_newton_c`, `_pcnr_c`,
`_tran_lte_c`, `_tran_radau_c`) hold the solver itself and read its numeric before each call; pcx_kluseq.h frees the
numeric a sequence replaces, on a serve and on a hand-back, and newton.c frees its chord's; `StructuralKLU.solve`
frees what its fallbacks replace.  The leaks: the plain solver's two overwrites, and every solver's end.

**Built**  `KLUSolver._free_numeric` / `_free_symbolic` (`klu_free_symbolic` declared beside `klu_free_numeric`),
`analyses_freed`, `factors_freed`: `solve` frees the factor and the analysis before a new pattern's analysis, the
factor before a residual fallback's; `__del__` frees `solve`'s factor and analysis and `factor`'s analyses -- none of
its factorisations is left then, each `_KLUNumeric` holding its solver.  `StructuralKLU` inherits the end.  `factor`'s
analyses stay one a pattern while the solver lives (its cache).

**Measured** (400 unknowns, each tree from its own directory): the plain solver over 2 000 alternating patterns, peak
RSS +115 -> +9 MB (1 999 analyses freed); 300 structural solvers made and dropped, +20 -> +4 MB.

**Tests**  test_linearsolver (+2): the plain solver frees the handle it held at a new pattern and at a residual
fallback, at its end the last of each and `factor`'s analysis; a structural solver frees its analysis and its last
numeric at its end.

declines, `radau_tc:klu_foreign` -- the numeric and the tolerance each call's), `_rk_back` (the numeric and the counts
as `StructuralKLU.solve` leaves them).  loop.c's transform mode: `tc_frozen` takes the fold's real factor's values at
the pattern once a step (`tc_rkgather`, `_ours`'s count: off it the attempt stops, `fold`); `tc_rsolve`, the early
check's and the estimate's real solves -- dgetrs on the kept LU, or `pcx_klu_step`; each attempt's sequence starts

## 2026-10-25 — 224. The NaN path -- the limiter's ranking sort is CPython 3.14's own list.sort, so a NaN key is ranked in C as Python ranks it and an iterate gone non-finite is limited in C: rich3 under Radau 4.86 -> 3.53 s (1.38x), gm1 1.20 -> 0.60 s (2.0x), every byte the same

**Why**  Andreas, on the survey after 221: "4 Do it" (plan g24's `plan_222_226.md`).  rich3 spent a quarter of its
Radau run in Python (25 % of its main thread's samples), gm1 most of its: the C limiter steps aside once Newton's
iterate goes non-finite.  LINE: rich3 under Radau at least 1.15x, gm1 not slower, every byte the same.  Refused under.

**Found** (sys.monitoring, nothing patched: a class-level patch made the C paths decline and the run 3-4x slower).
Each deck has ONE Python `_transform_loop` call whose stages went non-finite: 99 iterations, 297 limit walks, each walk
stopping at ~105 elements for the Python's limiter -- rich3 1.65 s of its 4.88 s solve, gm1 0.76 s of 1.20 s; 31 164
and 13 386 element calls (`climit:nan_key`).  No other gold deck has a NaN key.  The C limiter's laws already mirror
Python's `<`, `max` and `min` on a NaN (`_pymax`: `(b > a) ? b : a`); it declined a NaN key only for the ORDER: the
Python ranks the probes by `sorted(key=(-|vl - vn|, ra, rb))` (and the write-back's Kruskal likewise), and with a NaN
key every `<` is false, so the order is the one CPython's own sort leaves.  CPython 3.14's list.sort for lists under 64
(`count_run`, then binary insertion of the rest), modelled in Python, matched `sorted()` on 300 000 random key lists
of NaNs, signed zeros and ties -- once the test drew a fresh NaN object for each key, as the limiter's keys are (with
one shared `math.nan`, CPython's tuple compare finds the same object EQUAL: 69 % "mismatches").  The C consumers of the
walk already hand back on a non-finite limited vector (`newton.c`'s XNEXT check; `radau.c`'s and `radau_tc.c`'s STEP
bail in their scale loops, a NaN made by `inf - inf` their flags test): a completed walk over a NaN iterate hands back
where the stopped walk did, under another reason.

**Built.**  `limit.c`: `_sort_by` is that algorithm on `_tless`'s compares (the same order as any stable sort on keys
without a NaN; the compiled C matched `sorted()` on 200 000 key lists); the write-back's NaN decline only under
`PCX_NAN_DECLINE`.  `_hdl_climit`: `NAN_KEYS` (CPython 3.14), the kernels' NaN-key decline emitted, and the macro set,
only off it.  The Python's transform loop then walks in C -- the same laws, the same order, the same bytes (a NaN's
sign bit aside: unspecified by IEEE-754 and unobservable, `_compare`; no NaN reaches a result).

**Measured** (a quiet box, HEAD 4f91128f from its worktree and this tree, separate processes, interleaved, 3 rounds):
rich3 under Radau 4.86 -> 3.53 s (1.38x; the line 1.15x), gm1 1.20 -> 0.60 s (2.0x; the line: not slower), every round
within 0.04 s.  The gate's runs: rich3's process 1.38 s sooner, gm1's 0.6 s; the 27 decks' Radau solves 48.7 -> 47.3 s,
their gear2 solves as before (23.1, 23.3 s) -- no other deck has a NaN key.  The NaN attempt starts where it did: the C
transform Newton hands back on a flag of its own arithmetic (`radau_tc:bail:flags`, as before), and the Python's loop
now walks its 99 iterations in C.

**Tests.**  test_hdl_climit: every limiting library class, 600 random states with NaNs and infinities at random rows --

## 2026-10-25 — 226. A predictive step controller, measured -- REFUSED: the big decks' attempts +8.5 % against a line of 10 % fewer; nothing built

**Why**  Andreas, on the survey after 221: "6 Sounds good but explain more first", then "Yes, measure first" (plan
g24's `plan_222_226.md`).  24-27 % of the big decks' Radau attempts are rejected, nearly all for the error (early
aborts and the error test; Newton failures at most 101 of voter25's 2 408).  The stage family's accepted-step law
(`_StageSteps.judge`) is integral -- `h 0.9 err^(-1/p)`, bounded to [0.5, 2] -- so a run of good steps doubles until one
fails.  Gustafsson's predictive law (Hairer & Wanner's RADAU5) looks at the last two errors and steps and slows the
growth before a failure.  LINE (to propose building it, a C twin and a default change): the decks' attempts at least
10 % fewer in total, every deck's error no worse.  Under it: reported, nothing built.

**Measured** (a scratch controller -- the judge patched, so the runs take the Python path; attempts are what count --
on the 7 big decks at their own tolerances; 'reset': the predictive term left out on a step clamped by a breakpoint or
the bound, its history restarted):

| deck | today's (integral) | predictive | predictive, reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| ring | 5 775 | 6 187 (+7.1 %) | 6 187 |
| gm19 | 3 207 | 3 729 (+16.3 %) | 3 497 (+9.0 %) |
| arom | 3 704 | 3 969 (+7.2 %) | 3 900 (+5.3 %) |
| rich3 | 4 176 | 4 665 (+11.7 %) | 4 667 |
| voter25 | 9 657 | 10 451 (+8.2 %) | 10 563 |
| mux8 | 18 093 | 19 921 (+10.1 %) | 20 061 |
| jge | 20 386 | 21 603 (+6.0 %) | 21 649 |
| all 7 | 64 998 | 70 525 (+8.5 %) | 70 524 |

The rejections fell 2-21 % (ring 1 546 -> 1 223, jge 5 225 -> 5 083) and the accepted steps rose more (ring 4 229 ->
4 964): the law's caution costs more steps than the rejections it saves.  Accuracy against a reference at reltol x
0.01 (each unknown's largest deviation over the run from 1 % on, in units of `reltol |x|max + abstol`): mixed -- better
on some decks (rich3's worst voltage 3 006 -> 1 674, jge's 277 -> 225), worse on others (mux8's 645 -> 707, gm19's
'reset' currents 1 895 -> 3 367) -- no gain to set against the extra attempts.  (arom's reference run failed; its error
was not kept.  jge's reference took only 22 634 attempts: its steps are set by its breakpoints, not its tolerance.)

## 2026-11-02 — 228. Device bypass, measured -- REFUSED: on jge SPICE's check skips 42 % of device evaluations but its set exceeds the solution budget on 38 % of steps, every failure the stale CHARGES; nothing built

**Why**  Andreas, on the survey after 226 (2026-10-25): "Investigate 2 is there any references that we can use for
better foundation than just what spice does?" -- then, on the research, "plan and run it now" (the census; plan g24's
`tc/plan_bypass_census.md`).  The waveforms had shown latency on the digital decks: 31 % of jge's (device, step) pairs
with every terminal moving under 1 uV, 70 % under 100 uV (mux8 21/45 %, voter25 1/7 %, gm19 3/13 %).  Bypass changes
results within tolerance, so the question was whether an error-controlled rule would skip enough, safely.

**The foundation found** (full report with quotes, provenance and what was not verified: g24's
`tc/bypass_research/report_2026-11-02.md`).  Newton with errors in the function and the Jacobian -- Kelley, *Solving
Nonlinear Equations with Iterative Methods* (SIAM FA20, 2022, DOI 10.1137/1.9781611977271), Thm 1.2, `||e+|| <= K(||e||^2
+ ||Delta|| ||e|| + ||eps||)`: a stale Jacobian STAMP changes the rate only, a stale CURRENT or CHARGE moves the
converged answer by ~`J^-1 eps`; Dembo, Eisenstat & Steihaug (SINUM 19, 1982, DOI 10.1137/0719025) and Catinas's
perturbed form (JOTA 108, 2001, DOI 10.1023/A:1017583307974) for the residual budget, Eisenstat & Walker (SISC 17,
1996, DOI 10.1137/0917003) for the forcing term.  The integrator's side: RADAU5's iteration error at `kappa Tol`,
`kappa` 0.01-0.1 (Hairer & Wanner, *Solving ODE II*, IV.8).  Latency as a zeroth-order integrator under the LTE (Saleh,
UCB/ERL M87/21, 1987); a multirate interface's error, `(rho0/h) dq + di`, invisible to the LTE estimator and
controlled on its own (Verhoeven, TU/e thesis 2008, DOI 10.6100/IR631462, Thm 6.3); first-order bypass (Nye, ICCAD-88,
DOI 10.1109/ICCAD.1988.122543, abstract only); SPICE3's bypass and its failures (Quarles, UCB/ERL M89/42).  ngspice's
MOS1 bypass (default off) stamps the tangent at the old point; Xyce does not support bypass; two commercial
simulators' manuals advise against it for accuracy.

**Measured** (the census, `tc/census_b1.py`; Radau, 1 500 accepted step pairs per deck drawn with a fixed seed, every
MOSFET): each device's tangent error at the new point, its charge part through `c/h`, `c` = 4.06 (Radau IIA's largest
|eigenvalue of A^-1|), against two budgets -- per row `0.1 (reltol |J||x| + iabstol)` (the Newton residual test's
scale), and the step's whole skipped set, `J^-1 sum r`, within `0.1 (reltol |x| + xtol)` (the update test's, RADAU5's
`kappa`).  Two checks a kernel can afford: SPICE's (every `|dv| <= reltol |v| + vabstol`, every `|G dv| <= reltol |i| +
iabstol`) and a linear-change one.

| deck | row-safe (tangent) | SPICE's check skips | its set within the solution budget | linear check skips | within |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| jge | 99.5 % | 42.0 % | 61.7 % of steps | 77.5 % | 18.1 % |
| mux8 | 86.5 % | 9.4 % | 100 % | 26.3 % | 67.5 % |
| voter25 | 86.1 % | 0.5 % | 100 % | 10.6 % | 79.2 % |
| gm19 | 85.7 % | 1.7 % | 99.0 % | 29.2 % | 5.5 % |

The per-row residual budget is no guide: devices within it one by one exceed the solution budget together by up to
1e5-1e7 (its `|J||x|` scale is inflated by the `C/h` terms).  Split (`tc/census_b1_split.py`): of SPICE's set on jge,
the CURRENT part alone stays within the solution budget on 100 % of steps, the CHARGE part alone on 61.8 % -- every
failure is a stale charge, amplified by `1/h`, the worst at 10-100 fs steps.

**LINE** (set before the census): on jge an affordable check skips at least 30 % of device evaluations with its step
sets within the solution budget on at least 99 % of steps.  SPICE's check skips 42 % within it on 61.7 %; the linear
check 77.5 % on 18.1 %; on the analog-ish decks SPICE's check is safe but skips 0.5-9 %.  Refused; nothing built.  Not
measured, should it be wanted: a currents-only bypass (the charges evaluated every time) -- the split says SPICE's
check would pass on jge, but the fused kernel evaluates a call's passes under one mask and `G` and `C` share about
half their statements (`_hdl_cbackend`), so skipping `i` and `G` alone saves less than half of an evaluation.

## 2026-11-02 — 231. The device library's classes compiled on first use -- a class `elements_hdl` defines is created at import and compiled when first used: the library's import 0.169 -> 0.012 s, a short deck's process 0.730 -> 0.557 s, every result the same

**Why**  Andreas, on the survey after 230: "Do 1, then 2" (plan g24's `tc/plan_231_232.md`).  Process overhead (start,
netlist, exit) was ~0.74 s of each gold deck's process, 30-47 % of the gold suite's time.  Measured before building:
every gold deck uses 1-3 of the library's 51 classes (their creation 0.004-0.016 s), the import created all 51 (0.161 s,
the metaclass's compile 0.159 s of it, the class bodies ~0.002 s); and `spice_import` holds eighteen MOS classes in
tables made at its import, so a lazy MODULE would load them anyway -- the classes must exist at import, their COMPILE
deferred.  LINE (one form): a short deck's process (rca, start to exit) at least 0.10 s faster, the median saving over 15
interleaved quiet-box pairs against HEAD, every result the same.  Refused under.

**Built.**  `hdl.defer_compile(name)` / `defer_compile(name, False)`: the classes a module defines between the two
calls -- `elements_hdl`, its first and last statements -- run their declaration checks and stop.  Each of the 38
attributes the compile sets that the body does not (`hdl._COMPILED_ATTRS`) is a `_Pending` descriptor; the first read
of one, on the class or an instance, or an instance of the class or a subclass (`BehaviouralMeta.__call__`), compiles
it -- the descriptors removed FIRST, so the compile reads the class exactly as an eager one; a compile that raises
holds the class again.  The metaclass's compile is `BehaviouralMeta._hdl_compile` (was `__init__`'s body);
`compile_deferred(module)` compiles every class still held; `PYCIRCUIT_HDL_DEFER=0` defers none.  A class created in the
module's name after its definitions -- a collapse variant, a folded card's class, a test's copy -- compiles at its
creation as before.  The 38 names: the union of a scan of the metaclass's `cls.<name> =` targets and the names a compile
added over 62 classes; every compile records any name it set outside them (`hdl._UNLISTED`), and a test keeps that
empty.  The suite's conftest compiles the library at the session's start (the leak detector would see a class first
used by a test as that test's new state); `_testing.state.hdl_classes` passes over a held class.

**Found on the way.**  `_hdl_batch.generated_code` tells a generated method from a double by its code object -- read
off `BehaviouralMeta.__init__`'s constants.  With the body moved, every class read as hand-written: the evaluation
core, the batches and the C Newton declined everything, and rca's solve went 0.04 -> 0.34 s with every answer the same
(the Python paths) -- caught by timing the change before the gate, read off the paths' counters
(`once:core.build:unservable`).  It reads `_hdl_compile` now, as does the pinned pairs' test that each generated method
is defined once.

**Measured** (a quiet box, HEAD f1d92432 from its worktree and this tree, separate processes, interleaved, both warmed):
a short deck's process (rca, start to exit), 15 pairs: 0.730 -> 0.557 s, 0.173 s saved (0.151 to 0.214; the line 0.10
s); `elements_hdl`'s import with the package imported, 12 pairs: 0.169 -> 0.012 s. The used classes' compile and the
backend's first-instance work (the limiter's C source rendered, the libm check: ~0.05 s for a limited class) move from
the import to the first instance.

**Tests.**  test_hdl_defer (new, 9): the library's and the netlist importer's import compile nothing and open no
compile cache (fresh interpreters); the switch compiles at creation; each way in (a class attribute, an instance, a
subclass's instance, a name the compile does not set, `compile_deferred`) compiles the class and reads every one of the
38 names as an eager compile of the same model, its evaluations bit for bit; a compile that raises holds the class
again; no compile sets a name the descriptors lack, statically and over every compile of the process.  Three

## 2026-11-03 — 232. The limiter walk ahead on the pool -- every element's limiter made first on the threads, on the state as the walk found it, then the walk in order, an element on a node an earlier one changed made again; the pool its own unit, shared with the core: jge under Radau 12.83 -> 11.50 s (1.116x), under gear2 6.08 -> 5.36 s (1.135x), every result the same

**Why**  Andreas, on the survey after 230: "Do 1, then 2" -- 2 the limiter's kernels on the core's pool (plan g24's
`tc/plan_231_232.md`); after the sizing below, "build 232".  Measured (perf by thread, then DWARF-unwound so libm is
charged to its kernel): the `$limit` kernels ran serially on the main thread -- on jge 12.6 % (Radau) / 13.2 % (gear2)
of it in their parameter chains and their libm, 3.2 / 2.2 % in the laws, the ranking and the write-back.  LINE (set
before building, one form): jge under Radau at least 1.05x (the gold runner's solve, the median of 5 interleaved
quiet-box pairs against HEAD); GUARD: the 27 decks' total solve under Radau and under gear2 not slower; every result the
same.  Refused under.

**Found before building.**  The walk is ORDER-DEPENDENT -- `walk.c` writes each element's limited values back before the
next element reads (`SubCircuit.limit`'s loop the same) -- so the limiters cannot simply run in parallel; and under
Radau and the C Newton it limits each iterate against the PREVIOUS ITERATE (`radau.c`: `walk(..., yn, yp)`), so caching
the parameter chains per attempt is out.  But a limiter is a pure function of its inputs, its parameter row and its node
rows (local scratch, `static const` tables only).  A census (`tc/walk_census.py`: the C loops off, every 10th walk
replayed element by element on a copy with the C kernels, the replay equal to the walk in every case) found the walk's
writes almost never reach a later element: 100 % of jge's element evaluations would hold on the state the walk found (no
write-back of 25 749 gear2 walks or 66 435 Radau walks changed a node), 99.95 % of gm19's, 99.97 % of voter25's, 99.98 %
of mux8's.  Each C runtime unit has ONE entry (`test_c_abi`), so the walk could not reach the core's pool: the pool
became its own unit.

**Built.**  `csrc/pool.c` (`pcx_pool(range, ctx, n, nthreads)`): `core.c`'s pool moved out and made generic -- a job's
items in chunks of four from one counter on the caller and its workers (`pcx-core`), the caller's FP environment taken
and the workers' flags raised back, one call at a time, a forked child's own workers, the library pinned;
`_tran_core.pool_address`.  `core.c` makes its fused groups through it (`hdl_core_t.pool_fn`, `fused_range`; POOL_MIN 16
its own).  `walk.c`: where the walk's context wires the pool (`_hdl_climit._Walk.ctx`: `pool_address`, the core's
`THREADS`, a results buffer at each element's node-map offset and a return each) and a run is WALK_POOL_MIN (16)
elements or more, `walk_range` makes every element's limiter on the threads into the buffers, and `walk_ahead` walks in
order: an element none of whose nodes an earlier one changed -- its written value's bits not the value it found -- takes
its result as made (the same inputs the walk alone gives it), any other is made again in turn, and past WALK_DIRTY_MAX
(64) changed nodes every later one; else `walk_alone`, the walk as it was.  `walk_fn_t` takes the context: `newton.c`,
`radau.c`, `radau_tc.c` and `dcnewton.c` pass `wctx` (`_tran_newton_c._walk_ready` sets it, the transform loop copies
it).  The walk's flags are a superset of the walk alone's where an element is made twice or past a stop; every C caller
clears them untested and the C Newton tests none -- a test holds the callers to it.  `doc/transient_runtime.md`: the
pool's row.

**Measured** (a quiet box, HEAD 577f770b from its worktree and this tree, interleaved, after a warm run of each): jge
under Radau, 5 pairs: 12.829 -> 11.497 s (medians), 1.116x (1.096 to 1.130; the line 1.05x); under gear2 6.081 -> 5.363
s, 1.135x (1.125 to 1.139).  The gate's interleaved runs (a busier box): the 27 decks' solves under gear2 22.3 -> 20.7 s
(1.076x), under Radau 46.3 -> 43.2 s (1.072x) -- the guard met; by deck jge 1.13x, gm19, rich3 and arom 1.07-1.08x, the
smallest decks even, gm1 under Radau 0.981x the lowest (0.6 s, within that box's scatter).

**Tests.**  test_hdl_limit_walk: every test with the walk alone and ahead on the pool (an autouse parameter on the
core's threads); the walk ahead on 80 stages with a few nodes and with more than WALK_DIRTY_MAX written, on ten
inverters, stopping at a loop element and resuming, and on 200 diodes in series -- the only family found where the
past-the-bound fallback decides bytes (`pnjlim`'s answer moves with its input; a FET's laws mostly pass a value or clamp
it to a bound of the old one) -- each the walk alone's and the loop's bytes, `x0` apart and aliasing `x`; the walk alone
starts the pool's threads (a fresh interpreter); every C caller clears the walk's flags before any test.  Two mutations
of `walk.c` caught (every element taking its result; the bound's fallback dropped).  test_c_abi: the pool's unit and
`pool_fn_t`.  Pinned pairs: 21 twins re-recorded after the 945 tests of every C twin passed (`pcx_abi.h`, expanded into
every unit, changed; no reference moved); `pool.c` joined the core's pair and the walk's.

**Gate** (the main tree): the TELL (HEAD's walk alone, this tree's ahead, `pool_address`); the suite, 6 102 passed (10
skipped, 3 xfailed); the sanitizer builds, fast 5 881 passed clean, deep (the walk, the core, the loops, the pairs, the

Radau against HEAD interleaved: every digest, step, rejection, Newton count and path count identical but the loops' own.

**Found.** numpy's np.dot of a small matrix and vector is its OpenBLAS's dgemv (the core's call, equal on 20 000
products). Every order of a 2 x 2 row's terms, with and without a fused multiply-add, against it: one equal, `t = a1 x1;
t = fma(a0, x0, t)`; of a 3 x 3 row's 24, one: `t = a1 x1; t = fma(a0, x0, t); t = fma(a2, x2, t)` -- then `0.0 + t`,
the kernel's addition into its zeroed y (a -0.0 made +0.0). Equal on 120 000 random products of each size with signed
zeros, overflow, underflow, and a NaN or an infinity left in y; every other order unequal on about a third of random
products.

(the C library's `fma`, correctly rounded; the multiplication never contracted, -ffp-contract=off); else numpy's dgemv
as before. `_tran_core._small_gemv_ok(k)`, once a process at the first core with such a group (as
`_stamp_plan._matmul_ok`): the formula against this process's dgemv on 96 random products of mixed scale and 7 edge ones
(signed zeros, overflow, underflow), every bit -- 2 ms for both sizes; any difference, the dgemv. A product's lone -0.0
reaches no output (the bins add each slot onto +0.0, as bincount), so the `0.0 +` is held by the check, not by the
core's outputs.

## 2026-11-03 — 236. The held statements -- a class's kernel makes the statements no state reaches once a parameter state, into the element's pack, and reads them as loads after: jge under Radau 10.83 -> 9.83 s (1.106x), every result the same

**Why**  The survey after 234 (item 1; plan g24's `tc/plan_235_237.md`): about a sixth of a MOSFET kernel's statements
read the parameters and the temperature alone -- jge's level 3 class 100 of 624 (10 of its 48 `pow`), mux8's level 2
127 of 765 -- yet ran on every call.  235 left one kernel a class, so they are held in one place.  Ceiling first
(scratch `hoist/ceiling.py`: each grouped class's kernel and a copy whose state-free statements are loads, prepped
once): per call 1.05-1.10x for all four passes, 1.17-1.39x for `i|q`, which Radau calls most (counted in a worktree
core: jge 23.2 M `i|q`, 12.3 M `C|q`, 6.2 M all four) -- jge's kernel CPU by that mix 15.5 -> 12.4 s, ~1.08x the run.
LINE (one form, set before building): jge under Radau at least 1.04x, the median of 5 interleaved quiet-box pairs
against 235; GUARD: the 27 decks' total solve under each method not slower; every result the same.  Refused under.

**Built.**  `_hdl_cbackend.fuse_csrc(srcs, layout)`: a statement no `x[` reaches (through what it reads) is HELD --
`hdl_prep` makes them all, each in order, reading the held values it needs from the pack's tail and storing its own
there; a call reads them as loads under their runs' guards.  The tail's end (`HELD_TAIL`): the stamp (stored after the
values with release, read with acquire), the temperature's bits they were made at (another temperature makes them
again), and per pass the flags PCX_FP_FLAGS (`HELD_FLAGS`, a test holds them equal) the prep raised for that pass's
statements -- tested after each run of one set of bits, the caller's flags kept around the prep -- raised again by
every call wanting the pass.  The kernel's `p` is writable (`pcx_abi.h`'s `fused_fn_t`).  Every kernel object carries
its class's tail (`CKernel.tail`: the views, a DC-pinned class's second kernel's views, the limiter kernels) and
`CKernel.pack` sizes it, the stamp clear; a pack shorter than that -- made by another kernel -- is declined wherever it
is adopted for the class's kernel (`CKernel.__call__`, `Batch.run`, `_Core._check_elements`, PCNR's `point_packs`):
never written past.  A DC-pinned class's second kernel holds nothing.

**Flags, found.**  Against 235's kernel on 830 000 calls (the library's loaded cases and jge/mux8/gm19's classes;
every pass set; drawn and special states; each parameter zeroed, negated, huge, tiny; the temperature moved): outputs
identical but NaN sign bits (the backend's caveat); the flags a superset of 235's on every call, identical on the
elements' own packs with ordinary states; the extra ones only on inf/NaN states or moved parameters -- and at every
such case checked numpy's own pass functions raise them (or more), never 235's set.  235's kernel misses them where gcc
makes a `const` libm call only on the branch that selects its value; held, the statement is made eagerly, as numpy
makes it: at worst a needless hand-back (the flag rule), never another answer.

**On the way.**  The first build sized the tail from `info['_c_fused']` at pack time; test_core_fused's no-kernel case
(the info's kernel removed, the views bound) made packs without it and the kernel wrote past them -- heap corruption
that surfaced as a different failure in each of three runs of the twin tests (a PCNR DC test, a watch test, a JAX
abort) and as an ASan use-after-free in `hdl_held` from `pcnrdc.c`.  Hence the tail on the kernel objects and the
length checks above.

under each method not slower; every result the same.  Refused under.

**Built.**  `_cbuild.fma_flags(features)`: `('-mfma',)` where numpy's `__cpu_features__` -- what its own loops
dispatch on, the OS's register state checked -- has FMA3 and AVX, else `()`; `CFLAGS` end with it.  No result moves:
`fma` is correctly rounded by definition, the instruction and libm's alike, every other operation keeps its rounding
(`-ffp-contract=off` stays) and `-mfma`'s implied AVX changes encodings, not operations.  A CPU without the
instruction builds without the flag under its own keys, so it never loads an object that uses it.  Every key moves
once: the first process after this compiles the device library again.

The warm start-up without sympy -- a numeric run of cached models imports no sympy: the language's sympy classes and symbols in `_hdl_sym`, bound as stand-ins (`_lazy`) settled the moment sympy is imported, and the compile cache's trees apart, loaded on first use: rca's whole process 0.538 -> 0.348 s (1.530x), every result the same

cached models builds no expression.  A tripwire (sys.monitoring, warm cache, rca) and an Explore agent's map found
what forced it: hdl.py's module level (23 Function subclasses, `_IntermediateSymbol`, `Quantity`, `_StateSymbol`,
TIME/TEMP/FREQ) and the library's names imported from it; nine modules importing sympy at module level for use in
functions only; the cache entries' sympy trees (`sym_spec`, `pure_spec`, `pcnr_funcs`' sym/chain, `pcnr_affine`,
the limiter parameters' ingredients), unpickled by every read under `sympy.evaluate(False)` though only the JAX
twins, `explain()`, the symbolic toolkit and a limiter's C render missing its side entry read them; the key
(`sympy.__version__`, `srepr` of TEMP); `cls.linear` (sympy queries on every flat class build); lambdify's numpy
namespace taken from sympy.  All or nothing: one import anywhere costs the whole.  LINE (set before building; one
form): rca's whole process at least 1.2x against HEAD 5bf4dec8, the median of 5 interleaved quiet-box pairs, the
cache warm on both; GUARD: every digest, step, rejection, Newton count and path count the same on the 27 decks
under DC, gear2 and Radau; the suite; a warm run of a deck imports no sympy (a test).

**Built.**  `_lazy` (new): `module(name)` and `standin(module, attr)` -- the object itself where sympy is imported,
else a stand-in importing it on the first use that needs it (a call, an attribute, arithmetic either way, a
comparison, a hash, `_sympy_`) and forwarding; `isinstance` against one False while sympy is not imported.  sympy's
import -- by anyone -- settles every stand-in (an import hook on sympy's loader, taken down after) and puts each
target in its place in every module's namespace, so code that runs on sympy objects meets the real names; `describe`

`_TWO_PI` written in place.  The compiler: `generate_code` settles first; `_run_analog` puts a stand-in a body

evidence).  Census (counts, gear2): of every device evaluation, those whose voltages moved within SPICE's tolerance of
the last: gm19 61 %, mux8 56 %, voter25 59 %, jge 77 %.  A prototype (a worktree, `fused_element`) found the form:
outputs kept without a linear term stall the Newton (gm6 2 370x over tolerance); three references an element break
the chord Newton's contraction (the linearization's G not its frozen J's: gm19 22x slower); Radau's partial
evaluations as references cost 1.7-3.4x the steps.  One reference, linearized: jge gear2 1.32x at SPICE's 1e-3;
sized again at the analysis's own reltol (1e-4 on the gold decks) and 1 uV: jge 1.25x, mux8 1.04x, voter25 1.09x,
mux8 Radau 1.05x -- the idle devices pass on the absolute term.  The calls the prototype did not bypass, by pass
mask: jge 3.3 M full, 1.03 M i+q, 0.47 M G+C+q; mux8 Radau 0.72 M full, 4.7 M i+q, 1.3 M C+q -- the partial calls
writing G or C at another point overwrote the staging the prototype's linearization read: the reference keeps its own.

**Built.**  core.h: the bypass's fields (bp_at NULL: off).  core.c: `fused_element` -- the bypass armed and the
group eligible, `bypassed` first: the reference held, at the same temperature, and the first input and each other
input's difference to it within `bp_rt * max(|now|, |then|) + bp_vn` -> i = Ir + G dX and q = Qr + C dX (`linear`),
the reference's G and C copied into the staging where another call's are there (state 2), the element's count; else
the kernel, then `bypass_keep`: a full evaluation (every pass its group has) is the reference -- inputs, i, q, G, C,
temperature -- and a partial one that wrote G or C marks the staging another call's.  `_tran_core._Core.bypass(tol)`
arms (every reference cleared, the counts zeroed) or disarms; a group bypasses where its passes are all four, its G

`statistics.bypassed_evaluations`.  A parameter
changed during a run gives the circuit another core, unarmed: the rest of the run evaluates every device.
`analysis.py`: `bypasstol` (the Python `Diode`'s own cache) only where asked for by name -- it was derived as
reltol·1e-8 V whenever `bypass` was set, and its presence switches off the C loops, the C cache and the memos (a

0.992-1.000x, mux8 0.941-0.946x, voter25 0.933-0.946x.  Timed by phase (the same build, the pull serial against on

returned.  `get_threads()`.  Both exported by `pycircuit.circuit`.  pool.c, THE WORKERS A CALL TAKES: `pool_gen` holds the
generation above POOL_SHIFT (6) bits and the call's worker count below, published in one store, so a worker reads the
count of the very call it woke for (a separate count could be paired with the next call's job by a late worker); a call
takes its `min(nthreads - 1, started)` first workers (`pool_left` that many; the chunk from that count); a worker past
the count rests on `pool_rest` -- no spin -- woken only by a call taking more workers than the last (`pool_lastk`), so
a call never wakes the workers it leaves out; a worker's first generation from `pool_seed[index]`.  The docs:
`_tran_core`'s THE THREADS, `doc/transient_runtime.md`'s Threads row.

## 2026-11-07 — 284. The C transform loop's second fallback at a point keeps the point's record: an accepted fallback, then two stalled attempts, the first rejected, overwrote what the error estimate reads -- twelve rejections and a step of `minstep` on voter25; its Radau answer moves onto the Python path's, up to 93 mV; the other 26 decks do not move

**Why**  Found by the census of 283's item 2 (plan 261's L14): instrumenting the Python path gave voter25 7 330 steps where
gold has 7 232.  Not the instruments: `PYCIRCUIT_TCLOOP_C=0` alone gives the 7 330.  The gates compare a tree with the tree
before it on the same path, so a C loop parting from its Python twin on one deck is what they cannot see.  The two runs were
bit-identical to point 2 732 (t = 340.29 ns); there the C took a step of 1e-18 s, the Python 6.76 ps.

**The defect.**  The in-loop fallback has two coupled sets and writes "the set the last made fallback's is not in", and x_n's
record was documented as "in the coupled set the last made fallback wrote".  A rejected fallback at x_n breaks that: (1) a
step accepted through a fallback, x_n's record in set A; (2) the next attempt stalls, its fallback writes B and is rejected;
(3) the retry stalls, its fallback writes A -- over x_n's record, which `stage_estimate` then reads.  Each estimate after is
wrong, so each retry is rejected, twelve in a row, until a step of `minstep` goes through.  The Python's `_out` is safe: it
reuses a set only when no record holds a view of it.  Only runs with the in-loop fallback (up to 590 unknowns: `_sets_fit`).

**Fixed.**  `tc_fb_keep_x`: where a fallback is to write the set holding x_n's record (`fbx_set`), the record moves to `xr_*`
first, the buffers meant for it.  The sets' rule is kept: a stop still finds the last made fallback's set whole.

**Measured** (LINE set before gating, one form: on all 27 decks under Radau the C path's digest is the census's Python path's,
voter25 moved onto it, the other 26 not moving; gear2 and DC not moving): voter25 54b27d634a55 (7 232 steps, 2 396 rejections,
`tcloop_c:bail:force` 1) -> da7303d900cf (7 330, 2 438, none), the Python path's -- MET on all 27; gear2 and DC 0 differing; the
chain the same; suite 6 413 passed, 10 skipped, 3 xfailed.  Its waveforms move by up to 93 mV past 340 ns.
voter25 has no gold waveform; against its own run at reltol x 0.01 past 340 ns, the new answer's worst 100.6 mV (the old 125.4),
RMS 1.89 mV (1.99), the median unknown's worst 34.6 mV (34.0): a wrong estimate removed, not an accuracy gain to quote.

**Tests.**  test_tcloop_c `test_a_second_fallback_at_a_point_keeps_the_point_s_record`: voter25 to 350 ns with the C loop on and
off, the same bytes and statistics, no forced hand-back (before: 2 885 / 964 against 2 883 / 968).  A search for a small
circuit (`_pulsed` at maxiter 2-4, reltol 3e-4 to 1e-1) did not reproduce it, so the test needs the benchmark data.

**What the gates still cannot see.**  A C twin parting from its Python on a deck: the fixtures' twin tests do not meet every
sequence.  Comparing the 27 decks' C and Python paths (the census's digests, ~4 minutes) caught this one; not yet in the gates.

## 2026-11-08 — 293. `outputstep`'s grid made as the run goes: the run holds the grid and five points, not every step (keep fewer points, stage 1 of `tc/plan_points.md`)

**Why**  Andreas, "Do 1 and 2 then 3"; 3 is keeping fewer points.  A long run held every accepted state: the active 4 000-stage chain's Gear-2 10 us run 242 494 steps x 4 005 unknowns, 8.0 GB at its peak, so 100 us could not run in 30 GB.  The solver reads only the last three states; `outputstep` already reported a uniform grid, but resampled it after the run, from every point held.

**What.**  `_tran_grid.OutputGrid` makes the grid while the run goes.  The run tells it of each accepted point (the Python's accept, the C loops' write-backs through `_tran_loop_c._append_points`).  A point is finished once three more follow it (`FINISHED_AFTER`: the idtmod shifts rewrite the newest three, nothing else writes a past point).  When the finished points not yet made into the grid hold 64 MB (`GRID_BLOCK_BYTES`), `resample_uniform` makes the grid points at or before the last of them from those points alone, and all but the last two are dropped from `X` (their entries None: `len(X)` and the live indices hold, every reader takes the last three).  A run under 64 MB is one block at its end: today's call.  No new option; a run without `outputstep`, or on another toolkit, is unchanged.  `resample_uniform` moved to `_tran_grid` (re-exported by `transient`).

**Bit for bit, why.**  A grid point in `(t[j-1], t[j]]` takes points `j-2, j-1, j`.  A block from point `f` to `l` makes the grid points in `(t[f+1], t[l]]` (from 0 in the first), whose stencils lie inside it; `resample_uniform` on the block finds the same interval, and its clamps are the run's at the run's two ends.  The grid's times are numpy's `arange` from 0 by the step, which a longer `arange` starts with (40 000 random grids; checked again at every run's end).

**Measured.**
* Every gold deck under Gear-2 and Radau (54 runs) and chain 4000 Gear-2 1 us, mesh 63x63 Radau 100 ns and the active chain Gear-2 100 ns: with `outputstep` at tend/97 and tend/1999, with a block every step and with 64 MB blocks, the bytes of `resample_uniform` on the run without it.  57 of 57, the steps the same.
* The active chain's Gear-2 10 us run with `outputstep=1e-9`: peak **1 084 MB** (line 1.5 GB; 8.0 GB before), 242 494 steps, 115 blocks; the same run without `outputstep`, resampled as before, the same bytes (`a6406f7a1709`), its peak 8 723 MB.
* The gate against 8c727ef6 (`outputstep` unset everywhere): SAME -- 27 decks per group tree against tree, the matrix C against Python, 8 circuits at size.
* Timing, on a settled box: the default path against 8c727ef6, 3 interleaved pairs, chain 4000 Gear-2 1 us **1.005x**, mesh 63x63 Gear-2 1 us **1.007x** (line 0.99); `outputstep=1e-9` against none on this tree, 3 ABBA pairs, chain **0.998x**, active chain **0.998x**, mesh **0.994x** (line 0.98), the same steps, the active chain's 1 us peak 1 033 MB against 1 314 MB.

**Tests.**  test_output_grid (new, 29): the grid is the whole run's resample, every byte, on the Python's accept and on each C loop's write-back (the points through each counted), with a block every step and with one at the end, on a grid coarser and finer than the steps; the idtmod's rewrites waited for (one point sooner reads them before the rewrite: 20 of the result's entries differ); a run holds at most six points with a block a step; hand-made runs ending at `tend`, short of it, past it, a rounding below a grid point, and too short (refused as before).  A block that drops one point too many: 504 entries differ. ## 2026-11-08 — 294. `save=[...]`: a run keeps the signals named, at the solver's own timestamps; a transient result's currents made right where they can be, refused where they cannot (keep fewer points, stage 2a of `tc/plan_save.md`)

**Why**  Andreas: "For stage 2 save is good"; "Grid is something one turns on if one wants to post process with equidistant samples ... For normal analog work one wants the solvers own timestamps"; "The syntax ok.  We need charge device currents but it can come later".  A commercial simulator's way, read in its 2020 reference and 2004 user guide (`plan_points.md`): `save` names what a run keeps, a source's current is an unknown, a device's terminal current is made by the device during the run, only when asked.

**What.**  `Transient(..., save=['out', 'X1.n3', 'i(vin.plus)', 'i(R1.plus)'])`: a node's name for its voltage, `i(term)` for a current with the string `res.i()` takes.  Resolved before the run (`_tran_result.resolve_save`): a name that is no node, no terminal, or a device whose current the run cannot give is refused before the operating point.  The rows kept: each node's, each branch current's row (a source, an inductor, a delay line's port), each resistive device's rows (the hierarchy walked as `SubCircuit.extract_i` walks it, the device's rows alone), and the reference node's.  `_tran_grid.SavedRows` keeps them of each finished point (`FINISHED_AFTER`, as stage 1) and drops the point; with `outputstep`, `OutputGrid` makes the grid of those rows.  The result is a `TransientResult` (`CircuitResult`'s subclass): `res.v`/`res.i` of what was saved, anything else refused naming `save`; `res.rows` the run's row numbers, `res.saved` the names.  Default None: every unknown, as before.  JAX: out of scope (Andreas: "Jax can be out of scope now if it causes issues"); its results as before.

## 2026-11-08 — 296. A charge-holding device's current made during a Radau run: its collocation derivative on its own stage charges (keep fewer points, stage 2b's second half, `tc/plan_save.md`)

**Why**  295 made the multistep methods' and refused Radau's, the default family's: its derivative comes from the step's stages, which exist only inside the step.

**What.**  The stages solve `q(Y_i) - q(x_n) = h sum_j A_ij K_j`, so the step's end derivative is `K_3 = sum_j (A^-1)_3j (q(Y_j) - q(x_n)) / h`; `DeviceCurrents` takes it on each saved device's own charges at stages 1 and 2 and at the point (stage 3) -- its limit below.  The Python's accept hands the store the step and its first two stages (`_rk_Y`); the C stage family's accept (loop.c's `stage_accept`, the plain stage loop's and the transform loop's) copies them on the saved devices' rows (loop.h's `srows`, `nsrows`, `SY`, at the END of `loop_t`; the glue binds them per call from the run's store, `_tran_loop_c._stage_rows`) and the step into `SH`; `_stage_steps` hands them back.  Refused still: the other stage methods (TR-BDF2, ESDIRK, the GLMs: their end derivative is not a collocation's), the coupled family, a rewrapped state.  **Its limit, and Andreas's call.**  Summed over a node's devices the derivative is the step's collocation derivative of the node's charge, and the run's own end derivative is the equation's `-(i + u)`: the two agree only as well as the stage solve converged, divided by the step (the stage equations are in charge, `F = q(Y) - q(x_n) - h A K`, and the node's sum is `(A^-1 F)_3 / h`).  The multistep methods' Newton is in current and closes to the run's own row.  Andreas chose option 1 of three (ship, refuse under Radau, allow with the dense Newton alone): "1 In addition to documentation print a message" -- `save`'s Parameter, `DeviceCurrents`' docstring, and an `AccuracyWarning` once a run (`transient._RADAU_CURRENTS`).

## 2026-11-09 — 302. PCNR's DC clears each participant's kernel flags without glibc's x87 environment round trip -- the active chain's DC 1.10x at 4 000 stages, 1.078x at 8 000 and 1.087x at 16 000; every answer the same

`feclearexcept(FE_ALL_EXCEPT)` -- `fnstenv` and `fldenv` around the x87 status word, both microcoded, then MXCSR: 67 ns a call on
this box (fe_bench.c).  At c342744a the active chain 8 000's DC makes 9.31 M clears (an LD_PRELOAD counter: 9.2 M of them
`device()`'s), ~0.57 s of its 5.99 s; 4 000 3.22 M.  perf had put them at 2.8 % of the main thread: the microcoded stall lands on the
instructions after the call.  Transients make a clear once a pass or a step (the mesh's Gear-2: 122 k, ~8 ms of 4 s): only their
operating points gain.  Andreas: "Do F".

**What.**  `device()` clears with `pc_clear_flags`: `fnclex`, then MXCSR's FE_ALL_EXCEPT bits cleared -- what glibc's clears, every
flag `fetestexcept` and `fegetexceptflag` read the same after (`fnclex` drops x87's denormal bit too, which FE_ALL_EXCEPT excludes
and nothing reads), 15 ns.  Unconditional: the form that tests x87's status word first (4.5 ns) has an arm no kernel reaches (they
are SSE code), ~0.1 s at 8 000 not worth an arm no comparison can see.  Each asm clobbers memory, so it is ordered with the kernel's
call and the device's arithmetic as the library call is.  Off x86-64 / GCC, `feclearexcept`.  The unit's other clears -- once a
pass or an iteration -- as they were; pcx_fenv.h untouched.

## 2026-11-12 — 322. THE PACKED LAYOUT, P2c: PCNR's DC on the pattern -- its Python reference and its C -- and the standalone branch screen's C there; with it KLU's refactor check summed in one order on every layout (R)

**Why**  Plan 261 L20 (tc/plan_l20_packed.md).  Andreas: "do it" (P2c, P2d) -> after P2d, told P2c was larger than proposed and
gained no benchmark circuit -> "Build P2c anyway".  PCNR -- the DC's default chain wherever a device takes part -- did not
take the layout at all: its Python assembled J from the circuit's view (`pcnr_view`, another circuit object, outside the
packed scope) as a dense n x n matrix, wrote it in place (junction gmin, gshunt) and made the Schur reduction densely; its C
declined inside the scope.  At 32 768 unknowns and more a nonlinear circuit's operating point made n^2 matrices again.

**What.**  The Python reference (`pcnr`): the view's G assembled inside a scope of its own and put on the circuit's own pattern,
which holds every participant's places (`_packed_G`: the dense `np.array(view.G(x))`'s bytes at every place); the Schur terms
on it (`_schur_packed`: `np.add.at` / `np.subtract.at` at the pattern's places, in the dense form's order); gshunt
(`PatternMatrix.add_at`) and junction gmin (`_jgmin_packed`) at their places; `predict`'s gmin damper on the diagonal and its
gather of the kept rows (`kept`), KLU on the matrix's own pattern where no solver is given.  The C (pcnrdc.h's new last field
`packed`): the record and its core on the view packed (no |J|, dense or reduced matrix, no core C bins); the residual's scale
P's row sums themselves (`cf_packed`: within a row the CSC kernel's order, decided every time), the refactor's residual
PCX_A_PACKED; KLU on the structure whatever the size (`_packed.choice`).  The standalone branch screen's C on the pattern
(`_tran_branch_c._screen_packed`: branch.c's packed sets on the PatternMatrix's values, the diagonal through its places;
where the cheap level fires the Python's screen runs -- certificate, SVD -- handed back, `branch_c:bail:packed_svd`), and the
C loop's count of its screens back to the served ones.  The gate: ('dc', 'packed') in its matrix (the default chain, PCNR's).

**R: KLU's refactor check in one order.**  Line (b) first MISSED on opampal (below); Andreas: "Hold for a closer look", then
after the study "Fold R into P2c".  The check `not (max|A x - b| / max(max|b|, 1e-300) <= 1e-8)` after a refactor summed
`A x` in the CSC order in the plain KLUSolver, the walk, the complex solver and the packed layout, in BLAS's (dgemv) in
StructuralKLU's dense test, the chord's, and their C (pcx_kluseq.h's dense modes, newton.c's full Newton, lte.c's error
test) -- and where the residual is rounding itself the order decides.  A census of the 27 decks' default runs (~250 000
checks; the rounding bound decides all but ~1 000): BLAS's verdict parts from the CSC kernel's on opampal (16 / 8 / 8 in DC,
Gear-2, Radau) and e1480 (4 / 2 / 2, its bytes the same).  The dense result was not portable anyway: opampal's DC lands on
other bytes under `OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=SandyBridge` (42 fallbacks against 94) -- in both layouts, with the CSC rule too:
another BLAS reduction both share decides there; R does not claim kernel portability.  Now every layout's last resort is the
CSC kernel on KLU's arrays (`StructuralKLU._csc_residual`, `_csc_cols`; pcx_kluseq.h's `pcx_klu_resid_csc`, the dense test
and its A scatter gone, `A` and `dgemv` unread; newton.c's and lte.c's `pcx_csc_mv`, R no longer scattered or zeroed for it);
the rounding-bound passes stay first where they ran (their verdicts hold for any order, the kernel's too).  The chord keeps
KLU's values, not the matrix (`_ChordNumeric`).

**A gap the gate found, older than the stage** (94e24d09): the C loop put a full Newton's iteration-limit rejection's
